Photosynthesis Study Notes

Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. It occurs mainly in the chloroplasts of plant cells.

Chlorophyll absorbs light energy. During the light-dependent reactions, water molecules split and oxygen is released.

The Calvin cycle uses carbon dioxide and chemical energy to build glucose. Temperature, light intensity, and carbon dioxide concentration can limit the rate of photosynthesis.

A useful review connection is that cellular respiration releases the chemical energy that photosynthesis stores in glucose.
